purpose: Design baseline for AWSF v3: the Marimba panel and every surface the v3 spine plans, drawn before any of it is built so the built product can be compared against it. AWSF reads version, frames[].id, frames[].image and ticketFrames. Every other field is for people and is ignored by the host.

source.why: The canvas source is tracked, so a worker can read exact colours, sizes, words and the code of the two shared components from its own worktree. Images stay in the ignored docs/design/ tree and reach a worker through the owner’s binding. These digests prove that a later capture is byte-identical to the baseline.

mirror.why: 27 boards generated from this canvas. Edit this canvas only.

capture.method: Each board runs in the Design runtime with window.__pendulumStill set, which gives every pendulum one fixed pose from a seed. Each board is captured once whole. A board taller than 1,040 px is then cut into 1:1 pieces of at most 1,000 px, between sections where the page has a gap. Two full runs gave 275 identical files.
capture.viewport: Each board at its canvas size: 1440 px wide for dashboard screens, 430 x 884 for the phone, 1940 x 460 for the watch.
capture.limits: Every image is at most 2,000 px on an edge and 4 MiB, as core/src/contracts/visual-references.ts requires.

comparison: Facts: a screen is compared by the facts in frame-facts.json first. Each has an id, a kind of check and one sentence.
Glass: about 42 soft dots of 46-53 px at 14% opacity and 4 brighter dots at 17%, under a 165-degree tint and a 118-degree sheen with a 1 px top highlight. No constellation lines.

Layout: the dashboard tab bar, then one centred column about 760-880 px wide for the conversation screens. Run, workflow and settings screens use the dashboard's page width, up to 1320 px, and settings keep their own rail. Every tab without an open thread or dock carries the strip of frame 80.
Type: Archivo for prose, headings and controls. JetBrains Mono for ids, commands, numbers and status lines.

Colour: one colour governs lanes and access. Orange marks what spends, what waits on the owner and a live lease. Lanes and phase kinds differ by shape and fill. The pendulum takes each palette’s ink (frame 81), and green shows that it is done.
Mark: the pendulum of frame 64, with its six states and listening layer (65 to 65c). Motion is compared with the component’s numbers, never with a still image.
Voice: the owner's messages are bubbles. Marimba's replies are bare text on the glass.
Owner acts: a button marked with a key glyph, signed by the owner's passkey, with the terminal line kept as the fallback. Signing on the phone waits for the passkey test (Q44, U1).
Numbers are not compared. Bracketed values are placeholders and the run data is illustrative unless an override names its source.
Pieces: a piece shows the same pixels as its whole board at full size. Select the whole for layout and the pieces for detail.

overrides.rule: awsf lease grant, awsf close and awsf release are proposed command names. The deep plans of W05, W03 and W13 decide the real names; the built screens show whatever those plans adopt.

Bracketed values such as [N], [REV], [TRAP-ID] and [USED %] are placeholders for data only built v3 has. Measured facts in the frames are as of 2026-10-02/03: 168k median prompt tokens per v2 driver turn, 22 stale branches, 226 linked worktrees, 2645 unit tests at 4de5ff0, Jev at $0.042 per million input tokens.
Task names, candidate SHAs, decision ids and times are illustrative, not records, except where O6 or O8 names a source.
The tab bar's links outside Marimba are stubs. The built panel lives in the existing dashboard nav.
Screens are drawn in Forest dark. The built panel supports the dashboard’s palettes and modes. Frame 81 gives the mark in every palette.

These frames draw journal data from sessions 36deb464, f59bab60 and e298c4dc and the D3 round 2 prove set, read on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20, with times in local time (UTC-5). Bracketed values are placeholders, the grades in the routes table are examples, and the plan-author frame has no run behind it.

FL1 to FL9 come from section 12 of specs/brainstorms/2026-11-09-liquid-software.md. FL10 and FL11 came with the run screens. FL12 to FL19 were ruled on 2026-11-24 (specs/brainstorms/2026-11-24-design-contract.md).
Counts, sessions d3caa395, 1645ba32 and 36deb464, and the three projects were read from the state root on 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-24, with times in local time (UTC-5).
Signing from a phone or a watch is drawn as the target. Until U1 and Q44 pass, the built screens show no runnable owner act there.
Stop is drawn, and no stop command exists (G4). W17 defines it: end the running phase, keep the worktree and the record.
The round, sources and agents shown are samples. Facts about outside agents were read from the web on 2026-11-24 and must be checked again before use.
These boards are read by builders. Nothing on them is drawn in the product.
